question.text: The current in a conductor is expressed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> is in Ampere and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is in second. The amount of electric charge that flows through a section of the conductor during <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is ____________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
For variable current, integrate to get the total charge flown in a given interval.q=∫12idt=∫123t2+4t3dt
